answer.rationale: Only one candidate is backed by a recovered primary source rather than a summary: exp_86 (shortened onboarding) shows completion +13%, time-to-value -2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3% — a lever that both defends the existing SMB base and compounds into sustainable qualified revenue. Promotional_pricing is explicitly ruled out despite being the intuitive competitive response: memory_73 reads as an unqualified success, but the recovered source exp_73 shows signup +31% and revenue +18% against 30-day retention -12%, with the acquired cohort not surviving first renewal. Matching a competitor's price cut would trade the primary objective (sustainable long-term qualified revenue) for a short-term acquisition number and would accelerate, not stem, churn among exactly the price-sensitive cohort now at risk. Referral_incentive (memory_57), activation_messaging (memory_91), and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44) remain summary-only; memory_57's 'no measurable harm to retention' is the same shape of claim that memory_73 got wrong, so none should be scaled unverified — though activation_messaging is the strongest second candidate if next week's archive access confirms it. Scale is a standard experiment rather than broad rollout because exp_86 was measured on self-serve accounts under normal conditions, not on a base under active price attack; the retention effect may not transfer. DOWNSTREAM RISK FLAGGED: memory_73 is a lossy consolidation that dropped a material negative finding and would lead a future agent straight into discounting under exactly this kind of pressure. It should be rewritten to carry the -12% retention result and the explicit do-not-generalize conclusion before the next cycle. Verification budget is spent, so this decision is made under acknowledged uncertainty on four of five candidates.
